skill.name: swarm-orchestration
skill.description: Plan and coordinate agentic-flow swarms for parallel tasks, topology selection, shared memory, hooks, load balancing, and resilient agent workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate agentic-flow swarms with documented topologies, task modes, memory sharing, hooks, and resilience patterns.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences. Two alerts are confirmed because the skill instructs users or agents to run unpinned npx agentic-flow commands, which execute a third-party CLI locally. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, network beacon, or system reconnaissance intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the agentic-flow package version and require explicit user confirmation before any npx command runs.

remediation.issue: Hook commands may touch task or session state
remediation.suggestion: Document what each hook reads and writes, then ask users to approve pre-task, post-task, and session-restore commands.

content.value_statement: Coordinating many agents is hard when roles, topology, and task flow are unclear. This skill provides swarm patterns, hook workflows, and coordination practices for agentic-flow.
actual_capabilities: Shows mesh, hierarchical, and adaptive topology patterns for agentic-flow swarms.
Documents agent spawn and task orchestration commands using agentic-flow hooks.
Provides examples for parallel, pipeline, and adaptive task execution.
Explains shared swarm memory for storing and retrieving coordination state.
Covers load balancing, fault tolerance, metrics, and hook-based synchronization.
limitations: Requires agentic-flow and Node.js to run the documented commands.
Examples are guidance snippets, not a complete API reference.
External npx commands should be reviewed before execution.
It does not validate topology choices or performance results automatically.

use_cases.title: Plan Parallel Delivery Work
use_cases.description: Break a complex build into coder, tester, reviewer, and architect agent roles with clear task flow.

use_cases.title: Prototype Agentic Workflows
use_cases.description: Compare mesh, hierarchical, and adaptive swarms before choosing a coordination model for a project.

use_cases.title: Standardize Hook-Based Coordination
use_cases.description: Use pre-task, post-task, and session restore hooks to keep agent work synchronized.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a Small Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to plan a three-agent mesh swarm for [project]. Include roles, topology, and setup commands.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Parallel Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a parallel swarm workflow for [goal]. Assign agents, define deliverables, and include timeout guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Add Memory and Hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this swarm plan with shared memory keys and pre-task, post-task, and session restore hooks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Resilient Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an adaptive swarm for [complex system]. Include load balancing, failure recovery, metrics, and approval points for commands.

output_examples.input: Plan a swarm for building a REST API with tests.
output: Recommended topology: hierarchical with an architect coordinator.
Agents: backend coder, test engineer, reviewer, and documentation writer.
Execution mode: pipeline for design, implementation, testing, and review.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow swarm that has uneven agent workloads.
output: Switch to adaptive topology for workload-sensitive coordination.
Enable dynamic load balancing and monitor queue length, latency, and success rate.
Set timeouts and retry limits before expanding the agent count.

best_practices: Start with two or three agents before scaling the swarm.
Share key context through swarm memory instead of repeating instructions.
Review external hook commands before allowing them to run.
anti_patterns: Spawning many agents before defining clear responsibilities.
Using adaptive orchestration without timeouts or quality constraints.
Running hook commands without understanding their workspace effects.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate agentic-flow swarms, including topologies, tasks, shared memory, hooks, and resilience patterns.

faq.question: Does it require agentic-flow?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands and APIs assume agentic-flow version 1.5.11 or newer.

faq.question: Can it run tasks in parallel?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for parallel execution, sequential pipelines, and adaptive orchestration.

faq.question: Does it install software automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents npx commands, but users should review and approve those commands before execution.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides coordination patterns that can guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should users review first?
faq.answer: Review all npx hook commands, expected workspace access, and any session state handled by the CLI.
